translations.text: Love righteousness, you judges of the earth; think [?] of the Lord in goodness, and seek him with a sincere heart.
For he is found by those who do not put him to the test, and he shows himself to those who do not disbelieve him.
For crooked thoughts separate people from God, and when his power is put to the test, it exposes the foolish.
For wisdom does not enter a soul that does evil, nor does it dwell in a body that is enslaved [?] to sin.
For the holy spirit of instruction flees from deceit, and keeps away from senseless thoughts, and is put to shame when falsehood approaches them.

For the spirit of wisdom loves humankind, and will not hold the blasphemer guiltless for what his lips say; for God is a witness of his inmost being [literally: his kidneys], a true overseer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
For the spirit of the Lord has filled the world, and that which holds all things together knows every voice.
Therefore no one who speaks falsehood will be forgotten, nor will the judgment that convicts pass him by.
For the schemes of the ungodly will be examined, for his words will reach the Lord against his will, to convict him of his lawless deeds.
For a jealous ear hears everything, and even secret grumbling is not hidden.
So beware of useless grumbling, and keep your tongue from slander. For what is said in secret does not go for nothing, and a mouth that lies kills the soul.
Do not court death through the error of your life, and do not bring destruction upon yourselves by the works of your hands.
For God did not create death, and he takes no pleasure in the destruction of the living.
For he created all things so that they might exist, and the creatures of the world for life; there is no deadly poison in them, nor does Hades reign on the earth.
For righteousness is immortal.
But the ungodly summoned death by their deeds and words; they considered it a friend and pined away for it, and made a pact with it, for they deserve to be its portion.
For they said in their hearts, reasoning wrongly: "Our life is short and sorrowful, and there is no cure when a man comes to his end, and no one has ever been known to return from Hades.

For we came into being of our own accord [?], and afterwards we will be as though we had never existed; for the breath in our nostrils is smoke, and reason is a spark kindled by the beating of our hearts.
When it is put out, the body will turn to ashes, and the spirit will dissolve and [?] like the air.

In time our name will be forgotten, and no one will remember our deeds; our life will pass away like the trace of a cloud and be scattered like mist that is driven off by the rays of the sun and weighed down by its heat.
For our life is a passing shadow, and there is no return from our end, for it is sealed and no one comes back.
Come, then, let us enjoy the good things that exist, and make use of creation as in our youth.
Let us fill ourselves with costly wine and ointments, and let no flower of summer pass us by.
Let us crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither.
Let none of us go without a share in our rejoicing; everywhere let us leave signs of our merrymaking, for this is our allotted portion.
Let us oppress the poor and righteous man; let us not spare the widow, nor feel shame before the old man, the aged one of many years.
Let our strength be our law of righteousness, for weakness is shown to be useless.
Let us trip up the righteous man, for he is troublesome to us and opposes our deeds, and he reproaches us with sins against the law and accuses us of sins against our upbringing.
He declares that he has knowledge of God, and he calls himself a son of God.
He has become a reproof to us of the thoughts of our heart.
Even the sight of him is hard for us to bear, for his life is unlike the life of others, and his ways are different.
He counts us as loathsome and keeps away from our ways as from unclean things. He calls the end of the righteous blessed, he boasts, and he calls God his father.
Let us see whether his words are true, and let us test what his end will be.
If the righteous man is the son of God, let God help him and deliver him from the hands of his adversaries.
Let us examine him with insult and torture, so that we may know his gentleness and test how he endures ill-treatment.
Let us condemn him to a shameful death, for, according to his own words, he will be looked after."
These things they reasoned, and they went astray, for their wickedness blinded them.
They did not know the mystery of God. They did not hope for the reward of holiness, and they did not discern the honour of blameless souls.
For God created man for incorruption and made him in the image of his own nature.
Through the envy of the devil death came into the world, and those who belong to his portion experience it.
But the souls of the righteous are in the hands of God, and no torment will touch them.
In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died, and their departure was thought to be an evil,
and their going from us was thought to be their destruction; but they are at peace.
Though they were punished in the sight of men, their hope is full of immortality.
Though they were disciplined a little, they will receive great good, for God tested them and found them worthy of himself.
He tested them like gold in the furnace, and he accepted them like a whole burnt offering.
In the time of their visitation they will shine forth, and they will run like sparks through reeds.
They will judge nations and rule over peoples, and the Lord will reign over them forever.
Those who trust in him will understand truth, and the faithful will wait for him in love; for grace and mercy belong to his chosen ones, and his care belongs to those who are worthy of him.
But the foolish, who neglected righteousness and turned away from the Lord, will receive what their own reasoning deserves.
Whoever despises wisdom and instruction is wretched. His hope is vain, his labours are unprofitable, and their works are useless.
Their wives are foolish, and their children are wicked.
Cursed be their offspring. But blessed is the barren woman who is wholly undefiled, who has not known the bed in sin, for she will have fruit at the visitation of souls.

And to the eunuch who has done no lawlessness with his hand and has not plotted evil in his heart against his Lord, the chosen grace of faith will be given, and a most delightful portion in the temple of God.
For the reward of good labours is good and glorious, and the root of understanding does not fail.
But the children of adulterers will not come to maturity, and the offspring of an unlawful bed will be destroyed.
Even if they live long, they will be counted as nothing, and their old age at the end will be without honour.
If they die early, they will have no hope, and no consolation on the day of judgement,
for the end of a deceitful race will be [?].
Childlessness with virtue is better, for its memory is immortality, because it is known both to God and to people.
While it is present, people imitate it, and when it is gone, they long for it. In eternity it will be glorified with crowns, having won the contest along with those who are without sin.
The large brood of the ungodly is of no use. The offspring of adulterers will not sink their roots deep, and their feet will not walk carefully on firm ground.
Even if they put out branches for a time, they stand on a path of stumbling [?]. They are shaken by the wind and uprooted by the violence of the wind.
Their unformed branches will be broken off, and their fruit will be useless, unripe for eating, and good for nothing.
For children born of an unlawful union are witnesses against their fathers and mothers when they are judged.
But if the righteous person dies, he will be at rest.
For honoured old age does not come from a long time, and it is not measured by the number of days.
For human understanding is grey hair, and a spotless life is ripe old age.
He was pleasing to God and became beloved. He lived among sinners, and he was taken away.
He was snatched away so that wickedness would not change his understanding and deceit would not lead his soul astray.
For the envy of wickedness obscures what is good, and the giddiness of desire changes the minds of the innocent.
Brought to completion in a few days, he filled out many long years.
Because his soul was pleasing to the Lord, he hurried to leave the midst of wickedness.
But the peoples saw and did not understand, and they did not take such a thing to heart: that grace and mercy belong to his chosen ones, and his care to those who are worthy of him.
The righteous one who has grown weary [in death] will condemn the ungodly who are still living, and the youth who was quickly brought to completion will condemn the deceitful old men of many years.
For they will see the end of the wise man and will not understand what he purposed for him, and why the Lord kept him safe.
They will see and despise him, but the Lord will laugh at them; and after this they will become a dishonored fallen corpse and an object of reproach among the dead forever;
for he will dash them apart speechless, by craft [?], and shake them from the foundation to the end; they will be laid utterly waste and be in anguish; and their memory will perish.
And they will come in fear to the reckoning of their sins, and their lawlessness will convict them to their face.
Then the righteous man will stand with great boldness before the face of those who afflicted him and who despised his labors.
They will see and be shaken with terrible fear, and be amazed at his glorious salvation [or: life].
And they will speak in their hearts with repentance, and in anguish of spirit they will groan: "This is he whom we once held in derision and as a byword of reproach, we fools;
and we counted his life madness and his death dishonorable.
How has he been numbered among the sons of God, and his lot is among the saints?
We strayed [?] from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine on us;
we were filled with the way of lawlessness and of destruction, and we walked through trackless deserts, but the way of the Lord we did not know.
What did our arrogance profit us? And what help to us was that wealth of our boasting?
All of it has passed away like a shadow, and like a rumor that quickly vanishes;
and like a ship that passes through the surging waves of the sea, and no trace of it is found any more, nor the track of its course upon the waves;

or like a bird that flies through the air, and no trace of its passage is found; it labors with the beating of its pinions, and with effort it parts the light wind, it moves its wings strongly and passes through, and after that no sign of its passage is found;
or like an arrow shot at a target: it parts the air, and at once the air closes up again in the same place, and its passage cannot be known;
so we too came into being and ceased to be; and we have no sign of virtue that we could show, for we were spent in our wickedness."

For the hope of the ungodly is like dust carried off by the wind, and like fine frost driven away by a storm, and like smoke scattered by the wind, and it passes away like the memory of a guest who stays one day.
But the righteous will live forever, and their reward is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the Most High.
Therefore they will receive the kingdom of beauty and the diadem of goodness from the hand of the Lord; for with his right hand he will shelter them, and with his arm he will help them.
And he will take up all the armor of his zeal, and will arm his creatures for victory over his enemies;
and he will put on righteousness as a coat of mail, and set impartial judgment on his head as a helmet;
he will take up holiness as an invincible shield,
and he will sharpen unsparing wrath as a sword, and with him the world will fight against the foolish.
And shafts of lightning will go well aimed, and as if [shot] well [?] from the curve of a bow, from the clouds, they will strike [?] upon the target.
And from the rock, as from a bow [?], hailstones full of wrath will fall, and the water of the sea will rage against them, and the rivers will sweep them away without mercy.
And a mighty wind will rise up against them and scatter them like mist. And lawlessness will lay waste the whole earth, and evil-doing will overturn the thrones of the mighty.
Hear me, O kings, and understand; learn, you judges of the ends of the earth!
And give ear, you who rule over multitudes and boast of the peoples of the nations!
For your rule over them was given to you by the Lord, and your power by the Most High,
who will examine your works and search out your plans.
For you were servants of his kingdom, yet you did not judge rightly; you did not keep the law, nor did you walk according to the will of God.
He will come upon you terribly and swiftly, for a merciless judgment comes upon rulers.
For the lowliest may be pardoned in mercy, but the mighty will be mightily examined.
For the Lord of all will not shrink before anyone's face, nor will he stand in awe of the great; for he made both small and great, and he cares for all alike in advance.
A severe inquiry will come upon the mighty.
My words are addressed to you, O tyrants, so that you may learn wisdom and not fall away.
Those who worthily keep what is worthy will be counted worthy; whoever has learned these things will find a defence.
Desire my words, long for them, and you will be instructed.
Wisdom is radiant and unfading, and she is easily seen by those who love her;
she comes to those whose hearts have desired her, to make herself known to them in advance.
And whoever rises early to seek her will not grow weary, for he will find her sitting at his gates.
For coming to the heart [?]: to think on her is perfect understanding, and whoever keeps watch for her will soon be free from care.
For she herself goes about seeking those who are worthy of her, and in their paths she [?] to them with gladness, and she meets them in every thought.
For her beginning is the true desire for instruction, and care for instruction is love,
[love is] the keeping of her laws, and heeding the laws is the assurance of incorruption,
and incorruption brings one near to God;
so the desire for wisdom leads up to the kingdom.
If, then, you delight in thrones and tribes, O rulers of the people, honour wisdom, so that you may reign forever.

But what wisdom is, and how she came to be, I will tell you. I will not hide the mystery of God from you, but I will search it out from the beginning of creation and set out the knowledge of her plainly. And I will not pass by the truth,
Nor will I keep company with wasting envy, for such a thing has no share in wisdom.
A multitude of wise men is the life of the world, and a wise king brings calm to the people.
So be instructed by my words, and it will profit you.
For I too am a mortal man, equal to all, and a descendant of the one formed from the earth, the first-created.
In my mother's womb I was carved out as flesh, and over a period of ten months I was compacted from the blood of a man and from desire, with the coming of sleep.
When I was born, I drew in the common air. With the same suffering as others I fell to the earth, and like everyone else my first sound was a cry, the same as all.
I was raised in swaddling clothes and with care.
For no king has had any other beginning at birth.
There is one entrance into the world for all, and the departure is also the same.
Therefore I prayed, and wisdom was given to me; I called out, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.
I preferred her to dominion and thrones, and I counted wealth as nothing in comparison with her.
Nor did I compare her to precious carbuncles, for all gold before her is like a little sand, and silver is counted as clay before her.
I loved her more than life and beauty, and chose to have her in place of light, for the light that comes from her never sleeps.
Every good thing came to me together with her, and countless wealth was in her hands.
And I rejoiced over them all, for it is counted as wisdom [?]. I did not know that she was the [?] of these things.
I learned without guile, and I share her riches without grudging, and I will not hide them.
For she is an unfailing treasure among people. Those who have earned her have directed their learning toward God [?], for they were strengthened by the gift of instruction.
May God grant me to speak according to his will and to think in a way worthy of what has been said, for he himself is the guide of wisdom and the director of the wise.
For both we and our words are in his hand, as are all understanding and knowledge of crafts.
For he gave me unerring knowledge of the things that exist: to know the making of the world and the workings of the elements,
the beginning, the end and the middle of times, the changes of forms and the turning of the seasons,
the course of the year and the positions of the stars,
the natures of animals and the rage of wild beasts, the violence of spirits and the thoughts of human beings, the varieties of plants and the powers of roots.
I learned all things, both hidden and revealed, for wisdom, the craftsman of all things, taught me.

For in her is a holy spirit of understanding: manifold, subtle, moving well in every direction, distinguished and undefiled, spotless, clear, loving the good, swift, unhindered, doing good, loving humankind;
firm, reverent, free from care, all-powerful and all-surveying, and penetrating through all spirits that are intelligent, pure, and most subtle.
For wisdom is swifter than any motion and any instant; she reaches through and pervades all things by her purity.
For she is a breath of the power of God and a pure emanation of the Almighty, of the glory of truth; therefore nothing is mixed into her.
For she is a radiance of this eternal light, a spotless mirror of God's help, and an image of his goodness.
She is one, yet she can do all things; abiding in herself, she renews all things. From generation to generation she is given to worthy souls, and she makes them friends of God and prophets.
God loves nothing so much as those who are joined to wisdom.
For she is more beautiful than the sun and greater than every arrangement of the stars; compared with light, she would be found to come first:
for night follows after light, but evil does not prevail over wisdom.
She reaches widely from one end to the other, and she governs all things with sweetness.
I loved her and sought her from my youth. I sought to take her as my bride, and I became a lover of her beauty.
Nobility glorifies the one who lives with her, who prays to God; and the Ruler of all also loves her;
for she is the initiate in the knowledge of God and the one who discovers his works.
If riches are something desirable to gain in this life, what is richer than wisdom, which brings about all things?
If wisdom is at work, then who among all that exists is a more skilful craftsman than she?
And if anyone loves righteousness, her labours are virtues; for she teaches self-control and prudence, justice and courage, and nothing in this life is more useful to human beings than these.

If anyone desires experience, she knows the things of the past and infers the things to come. She knows the turns of speech and the solutions of riddles. She knows wonders and signs in advance, and the outcomes of seasons and years.
So I have now chosen to bring her home to live with me. I know that she will be my counsellor in good things and my comfort in cares and grief.
Through her I shall have glory among the people and honour among the elders, even though I am young.
I shall be found sharp in judgment, and I shall be admired in the presence of the mighty.
When I am silent they will wait for me, and when I speak they will pay attention to me, and when I speak at length they will put their hands over their mouths.
Through her I shall have immortality, and I shall leave an everlasting memorial to those who come after me.
I shall govern peoples, and nations will be subject to me;
terrifying tyrants will fear me when they hear of me. Among the multitude I shall show myself good, and in battle brave.
And when I enter my house I shall find rest with her, for there is no bitterness in her company and no pain in living with her, but only gladness and joy.
I considered these things within myself and pondered them in my heart: that immortality is kinship with wisdom,

and in her friendship there is good joy, and in her labour unfailing wealth, and in sharing the discipline of her care there is understanding, and in partaking of her word there is excellence. So I went about seeking her, so that I might take her for myself.
I was a [?] child, and a good soul fell to my lot;
or rather, being good, it came into a defiled body.

But I understood that I could not keep her by any other means unless the Lord gave her to me. It is the mark of perfect understanding to know whose gift this is. So I approached the Lord and entreated him, and said with all my heart:
O God of our fathers and Lord of mercies, you who made all things by your word
and by your wisdom created man, so that he might have dominion over the creatures made by you,
and govern the world in holiness and righteousness, and pronounce judgement with uprightness of heart:
give me, Lord, the wisdom that stands beside your thrones, and do not cast me out from among your servants,
for I am your servant and the son of your handmaid, a weak and short-lived man, lacking in understanding of judgement and laws.
Even if someone is perfect among the sons of men, without your wisdom he is counted as nothing.
You chose me to be king of your people and judge of your sons and your daughters;
and you told me to build a temple on your holy mountain, and in the city of your dwelling an altar, a copy of the holy tent that you prepared from the beginning.
With you is wisdom, who knows your works and was there when you made the world. She knows what is pleasing in your eyes and what is right in your commandments.
Send her forth from your holy heavens, and send her from the throne of your glory, so that she may be with me and labour with me, and I may learn what is pleasing before you.
For she knows and understands all things, and she will guide me in my deeds in holiness and guard me with her glory.
Then my works will be acceptable, and I will judge your people in righteousness, and I will be worthy of my father's thrones.
For which human being can know the counsel of God? Or into whose heart will it come what the Lord wills?
For the thoughts of mortals are fearful, and our plans are prone to error,
because the perishable body weighs down the soul, and the earthly dwelling burdens the mind that has many cares.
And with difficulty [?]
Who could understand your counsel unless you had given wisdom and sent your Holy Spirit from on high?
And so the places of the earth were set right, and people were taught what pleases you, and were saved by wisdom.
She protected the first-created father of the world when he alone had been created, and she rescued him from his own transgression.
And she gave him the power to rule over all things.
But one departed from her unrighteously in his anger, and he perished in rage along with the slayers of brothers.
For his sake wisdom again saved the earth from destruction, and she delivered the righteous man by means of a worthless piece of wood.

When the nations had gathered together, united in wicked counsel, she also recognized the righteous man and kept him blameless before God. She guarded him and kept him strong despite his compassion for his child.
She also rescued the righteous man from the ungodly who were perishing, as he fled from the royal [?] fire of the Five Cities.
Even now a smoking wasteland remains desolate there as a witness to their wickedness. Its plants have produced fruit [?], and a pillar of salt stands as a memorial to an unbelieving soul.
For when they passed wisdom by, they were not only harmed by failing to know the good. They also left this world a memorial of their folly, so that what they had sinned in could never be forgotten.
But wisdom delivered those who love her from distress.

When a righteous man fled from his brother's anger, she also guided him and led him on a straight path. She showed him the kingdom of God, gave him an understanding of the knowledge of holy things, and multiplied his labours.
When greedy men oppressed him, she stood by him and made him rich.
She protected him from his enemies and kept him safe from those who lay in wait for him. She appointed a mighty contest for him so that he would know that wisdom is mightier than everything.
When a righteous man was sold, she also did not abandon him but delivered him from sin.

She went down into the pit with him and did not leave him in his chains. In the end she brought him the honour of kingship and authority over those who had oppressed him. She showed that his accusers were liars, and she gave him eternal glory.
She also delivered a holy people from an oppressing race.
She entered the soul of the Lord's servant, and he stood against many kings with signs and wonders.
She gave the holy ones the reward for their labours. She guided them along a wondrous way and became a shelter for them by day and a starry light by night.
She brought them across the Red Sea and led them out through many waters.
But she drowned their enemies and cast them up out of the depths of the abyss.
Therefore the righteous took plunder from the ungodly. O Lord, they praised your holy name, and with one accord they praised even more your hand that fought for them.
For wisdom opened mouths [?] and made the tongues of infants speak.
She made their work prosper by the hand of the prophets.
They travelled through an uninhabited desert and pitched their tents in pathless places.
They stood against those who fought them and defeated their enemies.
When they were thirsty, they called on you. You gave them water out of a bitter rock, and from a fierce lion [?] you gave them relief from their thirst.
The very things that punished their enemies were the things that helped them in their need.
Instead of a spring from an ever-flowing river, the enemies were thrown into terror by foul blood.
This was a rebuke for the command to kill the infants. But you gave your people abundant water when they had no hope of it.
Therefore at that time you showed them, through their thirst, how you were tormenting their enemies.
For when they were tested and were being disciplined, though with mercy, they understood how the ungodly were being judged in wrath and tormented.
For some you taught and tested like a father, but those others you punished and condemned like a stern king.
And those far away and those nearby alike lamented in this way:
for a double grief took hold of them, along with groaning at the memory of what had passed.
For when they heard that the others had been benefited through their own torments, they recognized the Lord's doing.
For the evil that fell on them then: they gave him up and mocked him. But in the end they were astonished at how things turned out, for they did not thirst the way the righteous did.

Because of the senseless thoughts of their falsehood, which led them astray to worship dumb beasts, creeping things and contemptible birds, he sent a multitude of dumb wild beasts on them in vengeance,
so that they might know that whatever a person sins by, by that same thing he is punished.
For your all-powerful hand, which created the world out of formless matter, did not lack the means to send a multitude of bears or fierce lions against them,
or newly created, unknown beasts full of rage, or an outpouring [?] of fire and a blast of scorching wind, or the stench of spreading smoke, or terrible sparks flashing from their eyes,
which could crush them not only by the harm they did, but even by the sight of their faces, which would terrify them as they approached [?].

And even without these, they could have fallen by a single breath of wind, pursued by judgment and scattered by the breath of your power. But you have ordered all things by measure, number and weight.
For your great power is always with you, and who can withstand the strength of your arm?
For the whole world before you, O Lord, is like the tip of a scale, as nothing, and like a drop of morning dew that falls on the earth.
But you have mercy on all, for you can do all things, and you overlook people's sins so that they may repent.
For you love everything that exists and despise nothing that you have made, for you made nothing hateful.
How could anything endure if you did not will it? Or how could anything be preserved if you had not called it?
You spare all things, for all things are yours, O Lord, lover of souls.
For the incorruptible spirit is in all things.
So you correct those who sin little by little, and you remind them of the things in which they sin and teach them, so that they may be set free from evil and believe in you, O Lord.
For the former inhabitants of your holy land, whom you hated
for their detestable deeds, their works of sorcery and their unholy idolatries,
for their merciless slaughter of children and for eating human entrails and raw blood in the midst of your divine mysteries,
and for their presumptuous murder of helpless souls: you decided to destroy them by the hands of our fathers,
so that the land that is more precious before you than all the earth might receive a worthy colony of the servants of God.
But even these you spared, since they too were human, and you sent wasps as your forerunners, so that they might destroy them little by little.
It was not beyond your power to hand the ungodly over to the righteous in battle, or to crush them all at once with a merciless word,

but you judged them and from time to time gave them room for repentance. You were not unaware that their nature was evil and their wickedness inborn, and that their thoughts would not change. For they were a seed accursed from the beginning. Nor was it out of fear of anyone that you granted pardon for what they sinned [?].

Who will say to you, "What is this you have done?" Or who will stand against your judgment? Or who will accuse you over the destruction of the nations that you made? Or who will come before you to plead a case as an avenger for false men?
There is no other god who cares for all, to whom you would have to show that you did not judge unjustly.
No king or other ruler will be able to face you over those whom you punish.
For you are righteous and govern it in righteousness, and to punish and condemn one who does not deserve punishment is foreign to your power.
For your power is the beginning of righteousness, and your lordship over all makes you spare all.
For they show power, which is not believed regarding the power of perfection [?], and among those who know, you rebuke severely [?].
But you, ruling in power, judge with kindness, and with great forbearance you govern us for our salvation; for the power to act is with you whenever you will.
Through such works you taught your people that the righteous must love humankind, and you gave your children good hope, because you grant repentance for sins.
If you punished the enemies of your servants, who deserved death, with such care and entreaty [?], giving them a fitting time to be delivered from their wickedness,
how much more justly have you judged your own children, to whose fathers you gave the promises of good things because of oath and covenant?
You discipline us, but you punish our enemies ten thousand times more, so that when we judge we may be mindful of your goodness, and when we are judged we may look for mercy.
So those false people who lived in folly you punished through their own devices.
For they strayed far down the paths of error. They took as gods even those animals that are despised among their enemies, deceived like foolish infants.
Therefore you sent them a judgment that mocked them, as if they were senseless children. (26) But those who were not delivered by that mocking rebuke will experience a judgment worthy of God.

For the things that made them suffer and that angered them were the very things they thought were gods, and through these they were punished. They saw and recognized as the true God the one they had earlier refused to know. Therefore the full extent of punishment came upon them.

For all people are futile who lack the wisdom of God. From the good things that are seen they could not come to know the One Who Is, and since they did not look closely at the works, they did not see the Craftsman.
but they supposed fire, or wind, or swift air, or the order of the stars, or the force of water, or the lights of heaven, the [?] of the world, to be gods.
Those who delighted in their beauty and took them for gods should know how much better than these their God is, for the Author of goodness created them by his work.
If they were amazed at their power and working, let them learn from these how much more the One who made them is to be understood.
For from the greatness of the beauty of created things, their Maker is seen through the likeness of the things he made.
Yet the blame on these people is small, for perhaps, who knows, they go astray while seeking God and wishing to find him.
For they busy themselves among his works and search, and they trust what they see with their eyes, because what is seen is beautiful.
Yet even these are not worthy of pardon.
Since they were able to know so much that they could form a conception of this eternal world, how did they not find its Lord sooner [?]?

Wretched are those whose hope is in the dead, and who called the works of human hands gods: gold and silver, the products of craftsmanship, and likenesses of animals, and useless stone, the handiwork of ancient times.
And if some woodcutter sawed down a [?] tree well, and skillfully stripped off its bark, and with his art made it into a fine, useful vessel for the needs of daily life,
and used the leftovers of his work to prepare his food, and ate and was satisfied;
but the rest of it, good for nothing, a crooked piece of wood full of knots, he took and carved with the diligence of his idle hours, and shaped it with the skill of his leisure,
and painted it with red paint, and coloured it purple with crimson, and smeared clay over every flaw in it,
and made a fitting dwelling for it, set it against the wall, and fastened it there with iron.
He took care beforehand that it should not fall, knowing that it cannot help itself, for it is an image and needs help.
And he prays for his possessions, his land, and his children, and is not ashamed to speak to a lifeless thing.
For health he calls on what is weak, for life he entreats what is dead, and for a journey he calls on what cannot even take a step.
And for gain, work, and success with his hands, he asks strength of hands from the [?] firm one.
Again, one setting out for wealth and about to travel over raging waves calls on a piece of wood more fragile than the wood that carries him.
For desire for gain devised that ship, but the craftsmanship of wisdom built it.
But it is your providence, Father, that steers it, for you have given a way in the sea and shown safe paths on the waves,
for you are able to save from every danger, so that even someone without skill may go aboard.
For it is your will that the works of your wisdom should not be idle; therefore people entrust their lives to a small piece of wood, and pass through the waves, and come safely through on wood.
For in the beginning too, when the proud were perishing, the hope of the world took refuge on wood, and left to the ages the seed of a new generation, which was saved and delivered by your hand.
For blessed is the wood through which righteousness came about.
But the thing made by hands is accursed, and so is its maker: because he made it, and gave the name of god to the perishable thing.
For equally hateful to God are the one who committed ungodliness and his ungodliness;
for the thing made will be punished together with its maker.

Therefore there will be a visitation upon the idols of the nations, because among created things they became an abomination, a stumbling block to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the foolish.
For the beginning of apostasy is the acquiring of idols, and their invention is the corruption of life.
And they did not exist anywhere from the beginning, nor will they be
For through the vain imagination of men they came into the world, and for that reason a swift end has been sent upon them.

For a father, in untimely grief, was mourning his child taken early; he made an image, and now honors as a god one who was once a dead man, and handed down to those under him mysteries and rites of worship.
Then over time that ungodliness grew strong, and such a custom was established as a law, and by the commands of tyrants idols were worshipped.

Those whom people could not honor face to face because they lived far away, they portrayed that distant face and made a visible image of the king, so that with zeal they might flatter the absent one as though he were present.
After this, the ambition of the craftsman led even the ignorant [?] on to the command of the law.
For he, who knows, wished to please some ruler, and labored with his craft to make the likeness better,
so that he might draw the multitude by the excellence of the work; and the man who a little while before had been honored was now reckoned an object of worship.
And this became a snare to the world, because people, enslaved either to some misfortune or to tyranny, gave the name that cannot be shared to stones and wood.
Then again, this error about God and the ignorance concerning him were not enough for them; rather, they lived in a great war of ignorance, and they call such great evils peace.
For they hold gatherings, whether for the killing of children for idols, or for secret mysteries, or for the deceit of perverted laws.
They keep neither life nor marriage pure; moreover one man kills his neighbor or his offspring [?], or grieves him by adultery.
Everything is in confusion: blood, murder, theft and deceit, corruption and incorruption [?], perjury, tumult,
forgetfulness of good deeds, defilement of souls, perversion of nature, disorder in marriages, adultery and impurity.
For the worship of nameless idols is the beginning, the cause, and the end of every evil;
for either when they rejoice they are deceitful [?], or they prophesy falsehood, or they live by lying, or they swear falsely again and again.
For they trust in soulless idols; they swear wickedly and expect no harm.

But just judgment will come upon them for both things together: because they thought wickedly about God when they looked to idols, and because they swore falsely with deceit and despised the grace of holiness.
For it is not the power of those by whom they swore, but the punishment of those who sin, that always comes upon those false ones for the transgression of judgment [?].
But you, our Lord, are kind and true, long-suffering, and you govern all things with mercy.
Even if we sin, we are yours, and we know your power; but we will not sin, knowing that we are counted as yours.
For to know you is complete righteousness, and knowledge of you is the root of immortality.
For neither did the invention of men's evil devices lead us astray, nor the fruitless labour of shadow-painters, a smeared image changed with colours,
whose appearance arouses the desire of fools, and [?] desire to look at the lifeless image of the dead.
Lovers of evil, worthy of such hopes, both you who make them and you who desire them, and those whom you worship!

For the potter kneads the soft earth, labours, and fashions vessels of every kind for our use; but out of the same clay he fashions vessels that serve clean uses, and likewise all those of the opposite kind in the same way; what the use of each of these is to be, the clay-worker is the judge.

And with wicked labour he fashions a futile god out of the same clay, he who a little before was born from the earth, and after a short time goes back to where he was taken from, when the debt of his soul is demanded back from him.

But his concern is not that he will grow weary, nor that he has a short life. Rather, he has set his heart on rivalling the goldsmiths and silversmiths, he imitates them, and he has counted it glory that he makes worthless things.
His heart is ashes, and his hope is more useless than earth, and his life is more worthless than clay,
because he did not know his Maker, the one who breathed into him an active spirit and gave him the breath of life.
Instead, he reckoned our life a game, and this world a market for gain, for, he says, one must make a profit from anything, even from evil.
For this man knows better than all others that he sins when he makes fragile vessels and carved images out of earthy material.
All of them are more foolish and more wretched than the soul of a little child, the enemies of your people who oppressed them.

For they counted all the idols of the nations as gods, which have neither eyes of use for seeing, nor nostrils for drawing in air, nor ears for hearing, nor fingers on their hands for handling things, and their feet are useless for walking.
For a man made it, and one whose spirit is borrowed formed them; for no man can fashion a god like himself.
For he is mortal, and what he makes with lawless hands is dead; for he is better than the objects he worships, since he was once alive, but they never were.
And they even worship the most loathsome animals, which, when compared for senselessness, are worse than the others.
Nor are they even desirable to look at, as the appearance of other animals is better; for they have escaped both the praise of God and his blessing.
Therefore they were punished fittingly, as they deserved, and were tormented by swarms of birds.
Instead of punishment, you did good to your people, [giving them] food [?] of a strange taste to satisfy the craving of their appetite,

so that those others, when they craved food, would turn away even from necessary appetite because of [the creatures?] [?] that were shown to them and sent among them; while these, after being in want for a short time, would eat food of a strange taste.
For it was necessary that inescapable want should come upon those who oppressed them, and that these should only be shown how their enemies were being tormented.
And when the evil fury of wild beasts came upon them, they were being destroyed by the bites of crooked serpents; yet that wrath did not continue to the end.
For their instruction they were terrified for a short time, and they had it as a helper of life, to remind them of the commandment of your law.
For whoever turned to it was saved not by what he saw, but by you, the Savior of all.
And by this also you showed our enemies that you are the one who delivers from every evil.
For the bites of locusts and flies killed them, and no healing was found for their lives, because they deserved to be punished by such things.
But not even the teeth of venomous dragons overcame your sons, for your mercy was with them and healed them.
For they were stung to remind them of your words, and were healed at once, so that they would not fall into the depths of forgetfulness and become cut off from your kindness.
For neither herbs nor poultice healed them, but your word, O Lord, which heals all things.
For you have power over life and death: you lead down to the gates of hell and bring up again.
For a man dies through his own wickedness, and the spirit goes out and does not come back, nor does the soul that has departed return.
For no one is able to escape from your hand.
For the ungodly who denied you were scourged by the strength of your arm. They were pursued by strange rains and hail and unrelenting [?], and were tormented, consumed by fire.
For this was the most wonderful thing of all: in the water, which quenches all things, the fire grew even stronger, for the world fights on the side of the righteous.
At one time the flame was calmed, so that it would not burn up the beasts sent against the ungodly, and so that they might see clearly that they were being pursued by the judgment of God.
And at another time, even in the midst of water, it burned more fiercely than the power of fire, to destroy the produce of the land of falsehood.
Instead of these things, you fed your people with the food of angels, and without their labor you gave them ready bread from heaven, which had the power of every flavor and was suited to every taste.
For your power showed your sweetness toward your children, and it served the desire of the one who received it; [?] whatever he wanted, it took on that taste.
Snow and ice withstood the fire and did not melt, so that we might know that the fire that blazed up was destroying the crops of the enemies. It flashed in the hail and in the rains.
Again, so that the righteous might be fed, this fire even forgot its own power.
For all creation serves you, its Creator: it strains itself to punish the false, and slackens to do good for those who trust in you.
Therefore it was also changed in every way [?] and served your [?] gift that nourishes all, according to the will of those who entreated you,
so that your sons whom you loved, O Lord, might learn that it is not the growing of crops that nourishes a person, but that your word preserves those who believe in you.
For what could not be destroyed by fire melted under a small ray of the sun,
so that it might be known that one must [?] the coming of the sun to give you thanks, and meet you at the rising of the light.
But the hope of the ungrateful melted like winter frost and ran off like useless water.
For your judgments are great and hard to recount; therefore untaught souls went astray.

For when the lawless supposed that they held the holy nation in their power, they themselves were prisoners of darkness, held fast by a long night, and shut up in their houses, fugitives from the eternal [providence]. They lay there, fallen away from foreknowledge.
They supposed that their secret sins would be forgotten, hidden under the invisible veil of oblivion. Instead they were scattered, terribly dismayed, and terrified by rumours [?apparitions].
Not even the darkness that held them kept them free from fear. Howling sounds fell upon them and surrounded them, and unsmiling phantoms with gloomy faces appeared to them.
No power of mighty fire could [?break through] it, and no kindled fires gave light. Even the gleaming ones [stars] gave way to that darkness of the night.
Nothing appeared to them except the fire itself, full of fear. Astounded by the sight they could not see, they reckoned it worse than what they did see.
The art of sorcery and incantation lay fallen to the ground, and the exposure of their boastful wisdom became a disgrace.
Those who promised to drive away anger and terror from a sick soul themselves fell sick with a ridiculous fear.
Even a trivial sign frightened them. At the passing of birds and the hissing of reptiles they perished with trembling, and refused to look at the air, from which there is no escape.
For wickedness has its own fear. It is condemned by its own testimony, it always finds out evil, and it is hard pressed by its own suspicion.
Fear is nothing [but] the surrender of the help of the thoughts [?].
For the expectation of weakness lies within, and because of this torment it counts ignorance greater [than the cause].
But they, through that incorruptible [?] night, the unending night that came upon them from the depths of hell, those Egyptians slept that same sleep,
and they were pursued by monstrous portents, and the hope of their soul was undone, for sudden and unexpected fear fell upon them.
So whoever was there fell down and was held fast without chains of iron, shut up in prison.

Whether he was a farmer, or a shepherd, or a labourer in the wilderness, he was seized in the midst of his toil and caught by a distress from which there was no release, for they were all bound by a single chain of darkness.
Whether the wind whistled, or birds chirped on feathered wings, or an echo played [?], or water flowed rushing fiercely,

or there was a startling crash and the tumbling of rocks; or the unseen leaping of flocks, or the cry and roar of raging wild beasts, or echoes rebounding from the hollows of the mountains, it all undid them with fear.
For the whole world shone with the light of fire and was engaged in its work without hindrance;
but that heavy night was spread out [over them], an image of the darkness to come, by which they are to be seized.
But for your holy ones there was great light. [The Egyptians] heard their voices but did not see their forms, for they too were suffering, and they counted them blessed
because they did them no harm. Because they had earlier besought [them] [?], they gave thanks to God, and with joy they besought [them] for the [?departure together].

And instead of burning by fire, you gave them a pillar of fire as a guide on the way that they did not know, and you gave them a sun that was harmless and kindly during their sojourn in a foreign land.

For they deserved to be deprived of the light and to be shut up in darkness, they who had held your sons captive, through whom the incorruptible law was to be given and the light was to come to the world.

But when they plotted against the holy ones to kill their infants, and one child, whom they had cast out, was saved, then as a reproof to them [?] for their lack of love for the multitude of children, you destroyed them all together in the multitude of waters.
That night was made known beforehand to our fathers, so that they might know in their hearts whose oath they had trusted, and their heart would speak [?].
Your people accepted the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies;
for just as you punished the enemies, so you called us and glorified us.

For the holy children of the good offered sacrifice in secret, and in unity they laid down the law of holiness: that the holy ones would likewise share alike in good things and in punishment. And from then on they were already singing praises to the Father with laudation.
But the cry of the enemies resounded discordantly, and the pitiful sound of lamentation for their children spread abroad.
The judgment was the same for all, for the slave was punished together with the master, and the commoner and the king suffered the same affliction.
All together, by one name of death, they had countless dead lying before them, and the living were not even able to bury them, for in a single moment their most precious offspring had been destroyed.
Because of their sorceries they had disbelieved everything; but at the slaughter of the firstborn they confessed: "This people is God's."
For all things were enveloped in quiet silence, and the night in its swift course was halfway through [?],
when your all-powerful word, a stern warrior, came down from heaven, from the royal thrones, to the earth into the midst of the destruction,
a sharp sword, your unfeigned command, bringing death. It stood and filled all things with death; it reached up to heaven and it touched the earth.
Then suddenly evil apparitions in dreams terrified them, and unexpected fears came upon them.
And they lay fallen, one in one place and another in another, some dying, and each showed for what guilt he was dying.
For the visions troubled them, and you told them this beforehand, so that they would not be ignorant of why they were suffering evil and perishing.
The trial of death touched the righteous also, and there was a slaughter of a multitude in the wilderness; but the wrath did not last long,

for a blameless man hastened and fought. With the weapon of his own ministry, prayer and incense, he brought relief and withstood the anger. He put an end to it, and by this he showed this calamity that he was your servant.
And he overcame the people [?], not by bodily strength nor by the help of weapons. Instead, by a word he subdued the destroyer, recalling the oaths and covenants of the fathers.
When the dead had suddenly fallen in heaps one upon another, he stood between, held back the onslaught, and cut off its way to the living.
For on his robe reaching to the feet was the whole world, and the glories of the fathers were engraved on the four rows of precious stones, and your majesty was on the diadem of his head.
The destroyer yielded to these things, and they were afraid of them, for the mere test of the wrath was enough.
But upon the ungodly came wholly merciless anger, for he knew beforehand what they would do afterward:
that they would turn back again and attack them. Having quickly sent them away, they would repent and pursue them.

For while the mourning was still in their hearts, and they were thinking of the graves of the dead, they then devised another foolish plan; and those whom they had driven out with entreaties, they pursued again as fugitives.

For the end they deserved, which they did not want, was drawing them on. They forgot what had happened to them before, so that they would fulfil the deserved torment that was still lacking from their punishment.
And your people would experience a glorious journey, but they would find a strange death.
For all creation was being fashioned anew from above, each in a single form, and served your command, so that your servants might be kept unharmed by it.

There was the cloud that overshadowed the camp. Where the sea had held water before, dry land appeared to sight. Out of the Red Sea came an unhindered way, and out of the fierce waves came a grassy plain.
Through it the whole nation passed, covered by your hand, and they saw wondrous signs.
For they grazed like horses and leapt like lambs, and they praised you, Lord, who had delivered them.
For they still remembered their sojourning: how instead of bearing cattle the earth brought forth gnats, and instead of fish of the water the river brought forth a swarm [?] of frogs.
And at last they saw a new kind of birds, when, overcome by desire, they asked for luxurious food;
for quails came up from the sea to comfort them.
But punishments came upon the sinners, and not without the fierce signs that had happened before. They suffered this justly for their own wickedness, for they practised a bitter hatred of strangers.
Others did not receive strangers who came to them unknown, but these enslaved strangers who were their benefactors.
And not only that: there was also another kind of regard for those others, for they received the strangers grudgingly [?];
but these, after welcoming them with festivities, afflicted with hard labours those who had already shared in their own rights.
So they were punished with blindness, like those at the doors of the righteous man, when they were surrounded by boundless darkness and each one searched for the door of his own house.

For because of them the orders [of creation] were changing places, as the things spoken on the psaltery [?] in the name of the knee [?] unchangingly all [?] the groan [?], which is truly to be likened to the appearance of the things that happened. [The text of this verse is garbled.]
For land creatures were turned into water creatures, and the swimming things came out onto the land.
Fire overcame the water by its own power, and the quenching power of the water was forgotten.
Again, the flame that blazed up among animals that burn easily did not consume the flesh of those walking about in it. Nor did it melt the easily melted, ice-like kind of heavenly food.

For in all things, Lord, you have magnified and glorified your people, and you have not neglected them. At every time and in every place you have stood by them, for yours is the glory forever and ever. Amen. Glory to God. The Wisdom of Solomon is finished. Chapter 4.
